solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Poor, cutting short stag party (4,2)

indicatorNotes.cutting short: to cut something short is to lop off its end

blocks.note: a HART is a male deer, docked of its last letter
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

annotation.surface: Someone too broke to go on a full stag night trims it back.
annotation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British bachelor party, which is why 'stag party' reads as one phrase; it splits into the deer and the political party.
annotation.definitionFit: Hard up means short of money, i.e. poor.

entries.clue: Given assurance, from public library order in a book (6)

indicatorNotes.in: puts the first pieces inside the letters for 'a book'

blocks.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour

annotation.surface: Someone is reassured by finding a book shelved in its proper order at the public library.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' here is an honour, not a sequence: the OM is the Order of Merit, awarded by the British monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance, calm confidence.

entries.clue: Decline appointment, keeping outside but dropping by (11)

indicatorNotes.keeping: DATE holds the other piece within it
indicatorNotes.dropping: the letter for 'by' is let fall from EXTERIOR

blocks.note: EXTERIOR (outside) without X, the multiplication sign read as 'by'

annotation.surface: Someone turns down a job offer that would keep them out of the office.
annotation.walkthrough: X = 'by' comes from multiplication (three by four); 'keeping' then wraps DATE around what remains of EXTERIOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to decline is to worsen gradually, as health or standards do.

entries.clue: Confine confusion in magic diagram (9)

blocks.note: to pen is to shut in

annotation.surface: Someone is trapped in bewilderment by a magic square or diagram.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'confine' and 'confusion' together as a phrase, but each is simply a piece in turn.
annotation.definitionFit: A pentangle is a five-pointed star used as a magic symbol.

entries.clue: Judges restricted choice of dessert? (8)

blocks.note: the formal title of senior judges
'restricted' = only, and ices are frozen desserts: nothing but those on offer

annotation.surface: Judges limit the puddings on offer.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second half as a pun: split the answer as JUST ICES and it is a very short dessert menu.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: senior judges hold the title Justice, and 'just ices' is a menu offering only ices.

entries.clue: Revolutionary task acquiring current home (7)

indicatorNotes.acquiring: JOB takes the current symbol inside it

annotation.surface: A radical job means taking the electricity supply into one's own house.
annotation.walkthrough: The Jacobins were the radical club of the French Revolution.
annotation.definitionFit: A Jacobin was a French revolutionary, and the word means any extreme radical.

entries.clue: Secret police having initially hunted for one secret store (5)

indicatorNotes.for: that letter stands in place of the I

blocks.note: Roman numeral one, which H replaces

annotation.surface: Secret police search for a single hidden hoard.
annotation.walkthrough: STASI loses its I (one) and takes H instead: STAS + H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hidden hoard of anything, from cash to sweets, is a stash.

entries.clue: Woman, Verdi heroine who loses her head (3)

indicatorNotes.who loses her head: a head is the top, so the heroine's name drops its first letter

annotation.surface: An operatic heroine is beheaded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woman' is a bare hint that the answer is a woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is simply a woman's name, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida.

entries.clue: Proclaimed aim to cuddle cat (8)

indicatorNotes.to cuddle: END wraps its arms round the cat

blocks.note: the ounce is the snow leopard

annotation.surface: Someone announces they intend to hug the cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is a big cat here: the ounce, another name for the snow leopard, not the pet.
annotation.definitionFit: To enounce is to state or proclaim.

entries.clue: Type of solid fish almost, not about to be caught (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: the fish loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means turned around, so the word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.to be caught: the reversed word is caught inside the fish

annotation.surface: Someone describes a firm fish that is nearly, but not quite, caught.
annotation.walkthrough: The Platonic solids are the five regular polyhedra, cube and tetrahedron among them. 'Type of solid' tempts toward a state of matter; here it is geometry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by adjective: Platonic names one type of solid in geometry, the regular polyhedron.

entries.clue: Poorly dressed apparently in old kingdom (6)

blocks.note: the article in the phrase describing someone in tatters
a scrap of cloth, the garment of the poorly dressed

annotation.surface: Someone in shabby clothes seems to belong to an ancient realm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' warns that the answer is being read as a phrase: someone with a rag on is poorly dressed.
annotation.definitionFit: Aragon was a medieval kingdom in what is now Spain.

entries.clue: Conspiracy of silence breaks at Rome (6)

indicatorNotes.breaks: AT ROME is broken up and reassembled

annotation.surface: A plot of secrecy is exposed in Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: Omertà is the Mafia's code of silence, which fits the Italian setting.
annotation.definitionFit: Omertà is a code of silence among conspirators.

entries.clue: Person taking in hospital bible, showing proper demeanour (8)

indicatorNotes.taking in: BEING takes the other letters inside

annotation.surface: A hospital visitor with a Bible conducts themselves well.
annotation.walkthrough: The Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible is a standard crossword abbreviation. The comma marks the switch to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Behaving means acting properly, showing good manners.

entries.clue: Sadly unloved, me: is no one ever to be in my arms? (5,2,4)

annotation.definition: Sadly unloved, me: is no one ever to be in my arms?

indicatorNotes.Sadly: the letters are in a sorry state and must be rearranged

annotation.surface: A lonely voice laments that nobody will ever be held in its arms.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the famous armless statue speaking: she has no arms, so no one can ever be in them.
annotation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is the ancient Greek statue that has lost its arms.

entries.clue: Street musician after endless wild party more annoyed to secure no date (5,7)

blocks.note: the abbreviation for 'no date' in citations

annotation.surface: A busker becomes crosser after an orgy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No date' is the abbreviation bibliographies use for an undated work. 'After' is only glue between definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the organ grinder was a busker cranking a barrel organ, often with a monkey.

entries.clue: With no end of space, looks for oil that may be on one’s estates (4,5)

annotation.definition: that may be on one’s estates

blocks.note: fracking extracts oil and gas from rock

annotation.surface: Someone prospects for oil on their country estates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Estates' are estate cars, the British name for station wagons, which often carry roof racks; the surface wants country estates.
annotation.definitionFit: Roof racks are fitted to the roofs of estate cars.

entries.clue: Corps put up for such corrective treatment (8)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, 'up' reads the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

annotation.surface: An army unit is sent to get remedial training.
annotation.walkthrough: REME is a corps of the British Army, a standard crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Remedial describes treatment meant to correct a fault.

entries.clue: Organise meat to be cooked for unconventional household (6,1,5)

indicatorNotes.to be cooked: the letters are cooked up into something new

annotation.surface: Someone arranges a meat dish for an unusual household.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organise' looks like the indicator, but it is fodder; 'to be cooked' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A ménage à trois is a household of three lovers, hardly conventional.

entries.clue: Puzzle as small irritant’s overthrown sheep (7)

indicatorNotes.overthrown: GNAT is turned over, reading upward

annotation.surface: A little pest knocks over a sheep.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the gnat is overthrown, then the ram follows.
annotation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese puzzle of seven shapes.

entries.clue: Object to name having to be changed around (6)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means placed round the outside, so the changed word encloses the letter

annotation.surface: Someone objects to being made to change their name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having to be' is only glue; 'changed' gives the enclosing word, which takes the letter just before its end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to resent a thing is to take offence at it, which is to object to it.

entries.clue: A boy always safe with cooking equipment (5,3)

annotation.surface: A boy has a safe full of kitchen kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peter' is old criminal slang for a safe (safe-crackers were 'peter men').
annotation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up: a boy always.

entries.clue: Twist flipped over new cocktail ingredient (5)

indicatorNotes.flipped over: to flip something over is to turn it upside down, so the word is reversed

annotation.surface: A bartender tosses a new twist into a cocktail.
annotation.walkthrough: A prawn cocktail is a starter, so the drink the surface suggests is not the dish.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the classic British starter is shellfish in pink sauce, named for this ingredient.

entries.clue: Joint freer after manipulation, if energy put in (6)

indicatorNotes.after manipulation: FREER is handled into a new order
indicatorNotes.put in: to put something in is to insert it, so the letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: physics symbol, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A physio says a stiff joint moves better once some energy is put in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is not a knee or elbow but a cannabis cigarette.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: both words name a cannabis cigarette.

entries.clue: Agency arresting scoundrel, a chirpy type (6)

indicatorNotes.arresting: CIA holds the scoundrel inside, as police hold a suspect

annotation.surface: An agency detains a villain who turns out to be cheerful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chirpy' suggests a cheerful person, but it is literal: the cicada makes a loud chirping noise.
annotation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect known for its shrill chirping.

entries.clue: Back in first part of post-lunch period (3)

indicatorNotes.first part of: keep only the opening of the word

annotation.surface: Someone returns early in the afternoon.
annotation.walkthrough: The post-lunch period is the afternoon, whose first three letters mean 'at the back' on a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Aft means at or towards the back of a boat.

entries.clue: Radio is crook (8)

blocks.note: a set that picks up broadcasts
a criminal who handles stolen goods

annotation.surface: A statement that the wireless is broken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crook' tempts as British slang for ill or broken, but it is a criminal: one who handles stolen goods.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a radio set picks up signals, and a fence takes in stolen property, so each receives.

entries.clue: Choice includes a base metal or precious one (8)

blocks.note: a plum job is a choice one

annotation.surface: A choice between a base metal and a precious one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' means metal, carried over from 'base metal': the answer is a precious metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: 'one' stands for metal, and this is among the most precious.

entries.clue: Nervous, holding forth in loud, aggressive manner (6)

annotation.definitionNote: SHOUTY is an adjective; the definition reads as describing someone's manner.

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold something is to keep it in your grasp, so one word keeps the other inside

blocks.note: to go forth is to go out

annotation.surface: A nervous person holds forth noisily and aggressively.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holding forth' reads as a single phrase for speechifying, but it splits: the nervous word holds 'forth'.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial word: shouty describes speech or behaviour marked by loud aggression.
